title: Spinach and Feta Omelet
description: Fresh green spinach, crisp onions and a touch of creamy feta cheese make this an omelet you will want to prepare again and again.
steps: In a bowl, season the egg substitute with salt and pepper and mix everything together.
Heat the olive oil in a nonstick skillet over medium heat.
Add the diced red onions and sauté until softened.
Add the chopped spinach to the skillet and cook until wilted.
Pour the eggs over the spinach and onions.
As the eggs begin to set, sprinkle diced tomatoes and crumbled feta cheese over half of the omelet.
Once the eggs are completely cooked, carefully fold the omelet in half with a spatula.
Slide the omelet onto a plate, garnish with fresh herbs if desired, and serve.

title: Romaine Lettuce
description: One cup of chopped romaine lettuce

title: Greek Pita Veggie Pizzas
description: A tasty blend of Mediterranean style and pizza come together in this Greek pita veggie pizza. Packed with nutrient-rich vegetables like red peppers, olives, shallots and artichokes, this quick and easy recipe is ready in under 15 minutes. Try serving it with Mediterranean zucchini for a hearty meal.
ingredients: 4 small whole wheat pitas (4 whole wheat pita rounds, 4 inches each)
1 cup low-sodium jarred pizza sauce (1 cup low-sodium pizza sauce)
1/4 cup low-fat shredded Italian cheese (¼ cup reduced-fat shredded Italian cheese)
1/4 cup Kalamata olives (¼ cup sliced Kalamata olives)
1/4 cup roasted red peppers (¼ cup roasted red peppers, thinly sliced)
1/4 cup marinated artichoke hearts (¼ cup marinated artichoke hearts, chopped)
2 oz low-fat feta cheese (2 oz reduced-fat feta cheese, crumbled)
1/2 cup fresh basil (½ cup fresh basil leaves, cut into thin strips)
steps: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F.
Top the pita bread with sauce, olives, peppers, artichokes, shallot and Italian cheese.
Bake in the oven until the cheese melts and the pita is crisp, 7-8 minutes.
Remove from the oven and top with feta cheese and fresh basil.

title: Roasted Beet and Apple Soup
description: Earthy and slightly sweet, I love making this scarlet-hued soup in mid to late fall, when apples and beets are at their peak. It is the perfect starter for an autumn-themed meal, and its contrasting sweet and tart flavors complement all kinds of seasonal dishes, from pork and chicken to roasted cauliflower and Brussels sprouts.
ingredients: 1/2 lbs red beets (trimmed and washed (about 3 medium beets))
2 Granny Smith or other tart apples (peeled, cored and diced)
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F.

Wrap each beet in a piece of aluminum foil and roast until tender when pierced with a fork, about 1 hour. Remove the beets from the oven, unwrap them and let them cool for 5 minutes. Then peel the beets and cut them into 1/2-inch cubes.

Heat the oil in a medium heavy-bottomed saucepan over medium-high heat. Add the leek and garlic and cook for 5 to 8 minutes or until tender. Add the apples, the chopped beets and the ginger. Cook for 1 to 2 minutes, stirring constantly, then add the orange juice, the orange zest and the broth.
Bring the liquid to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover the saucepan and simmer until the vegetables are very tender, about 25 minutes.

Remove the pan from the heat, add the lemon juice and let the soup cool slightly. Carefully transfer the soup to a blender or food processor, in batches if necessary, and puree until smooth. Season with salt and pepper and serve immediately.

title: Moroccan Roasted Turkey Breast with Root Vegetables
description: Moroccan spices like cinnamon, cardamom, cumin and coriander are ideal seasonings for roasted vegetables and meats. During roasting, they bring out the sweetness and deep flavors of whatever they are coating, and their rich, warm flavors transport the taste buds to exotic places. Make this dish in winter, when oranges are in season and cabin fever has started to set in.
ingredients: 1 onion (halved, peeled, then cut into quarters)
3 stalks celery (trimmed and cut into thirds)
2 cups carrots (peeled, chopped and cut into 2-inch pieces)
2 cups rutabaga (peeled, chopped and cut into 2-inch pieces)
1 cup turnips (peeled, chopped and cut into 2-inch pieces)
1 cup sweet potato (peeled, chopped and cut into 2-inch pieces)
steps: Preheat the oven to 425°F.

Loosen the skin of the turkey breast by gently pushing your fingers between the skin and the meat. Season under the skin with 1 tablespoon of olive oil, 1/2 teaspoon of salt and 1/2 teaspoon of pepper. Rub the spice blend under and over the loosened skin, then place the turkey breast in a roasting pan.

In a small bowl, mix the remaining oil, the remaining salt and pepper, the garlic, onion, celery, carrots, rutabaga, turnip, sweet potato, oregano, orange zest, orange, cumin and smoked paprika. Arrange the vegetable mixture in a single layer around the turkey breast.

Transfer the pan to the oven and roast the turkey and vegetables, uncovered, for 15 minutes. Loosely cover the pan with aluminum foil. Reduce the oven temperature to 325°F and roast for 30 to 45 minutes more, or until an instant-read thermometer inserted into the meatiest part of the turkey breast registers 165°F.
Remove the pan from the oven, transfer the turkey to a cutting board and loosely cover it with aluminum foil. Let the turkey rest for 20 minutes, then discard the skin and slice the meat.
Remove and discard the oranges from the roasted vegetables, stir the vegetables well and serve them with the sliced turkey.

title: Peanut Butter Chocolate Chip Bars
description: I boosted this version of a "blondie" with the goodness of peanut butter. These bars are a great example of a dessert that is sweet enough, yet ridiculously satisfying!
ingredients: 1/3 cup pure maple syrup (preferably grade B)
1/2 cup peanut butter with no added sugar
3/4 cup chickpea flour or spelt flour
1/3 cup dark chocolate chips sweetened with stevia (no added sugars)
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F. Coat a 9 x 9-inch baking dish with nonstick cooking spray.
In the bowl of an electric mixer, or with a hand mixer, beat the egg, egg white, oil, maple syrup, banana, almond milk, vanilla and peanut butter until smooth. Set the wet ingredients aside.
In a separate large bowl, mix the almond flour, chickpea flour, flaxseeds, baking powder and baking soda.

Add the dry ingredients to the wet ingredients and stir with a wooden spoon or a spatula until well combined. Fold in the chocolate chips. Pour the batter into the prepared baking dish and spread it evenly.
Transfer the pan to the oven and bake for 30 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.
Remove the pan from the oven, let it cool slightly and then cut into 16 bars.

title: Oven-Fried Chicken
description: This "fried" chicken is not only healthier than traditional fried chicken, but also easier and less fussy to make than the traditional version.
ingredients: 2 cups whole wheat Italian-style bread crumbs
2 large eggs (beaten with 1 tablespoon of water)
steps: Preheat the oven to 375°F convection or 400°F in a conventional oven. Place the bread crumbs, garlic and stress-free Italian seasoning mix in the food processor. Process until well combined.
Place the flour in a pie dish. Place the eggs and egg whites in a separate pie dish. Place the bread crumb mixture in a third pie dish.
Line a large baking sheet with parchment paper.

Dip the chicken in flour and coat it on all sides, then in egg and then in bread crumbs. Coat evenly. Place it on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. If you have time, refrigerate the chicken for a while before cooking it.
Bake the chicken for 45 minutes until crispy and well browned. Serve with picnic-style condiments or salads. It can be made ahead and frozen to reheat in a very hot oven. Thaw before reheating.

title: Balsamic Salmon over Barley Pilaf
ingredients: 1 lbs salmon (skinless, cut into 4 pieces (4 oz each))
steps: Place the canola oil in a large pot. Heat and add the onion, garlic and celery. Cook over medium heat, covered, until the onion becomes translucent. Add the carrots and barley and cook uncovered until the barley begins to look toasted. Add broth. Cover and cook 30 minutes.

Cut the tomatoes in half and place them in a large bowl with balsamic vinegar, basil, salt, pepper and salmon. Let it rest while the barley cooks for the first 30 minutes. After 30 minutes, remove the salmon from the tomato mixture. Add the tomato mixture to the barley and place the salmon on top of the barley. Cover and cook 10 more minutes to steam the salmon.
Place some barley pilaf in a pasta bowl and top with a piece of salmon to serve.

title: Sweet and Sour Cucumbers
description: This recipe is presented by DaVita, a proud partner of the American Diabetes Association® and Diabetes Food Hub®
steps: The marinade liquid should be drained well and discarded from the cucumbers before serving. Serve in small salad bowls as a salad or snack.
Cover the container with plastic wrap and leave it in the refrigerator for the last 2 hours.
Pour over the cucumbers and onion. Add pepper and, if desired, ¼ teaspoon of salt.
Combine the sugar and vinegar. Stir until the sugar dissolves completely.
Cut the cucumbers and onions into slices about 1/8 inch thick. Place in a large bowl.

title: Sesame Maple Glazed Tofu with Veggie Quinoa and Furikake
description:
For this vibrant dish, you will brown tofu and glaze it in the skillet with a sweet and savory mixture of sesame oil, maple syrup and more, then serve it over a hearty bed of quinoa mixed with sautéed cabbage, carrots and mushrooms.

Blue Apron believes mealtime should be the best part of the day. That is why we partnered with the American Diabetes Association to serve delicious, ready-to-cook meals packed with fresh produce, lean proteins and plenty of tasty options. All delivered to your door.
ingredients: 2 tbsp coconut aminos or low-sodium soy sauce
steps: Cook the quinoa: Fill a medium pot 3/4 full with salted water; cover and heat to a boil over high heat. Once it boils, add the quinoa and cook, uncovered, for 18 to 20 minutes or until tender. Turn off the heat. Drain well and return to the pot.

Press the tofu: Meanwhile, drain the tofu and then place it on a plate lined with paper towels. Place several layers of paper towels on top and then place a heavy-bottomed pot (or skillet) on top of the paper towels. Set aside to release excess liquid for at least 10 minutes.

Prep the ingredients and make the glaze: Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce. Peel the carrots; thinly slice them on an angle. Cut the mushrooms into small pieces. Cut out and discard the core of the cabbage; thinly slice the leaves. Peel and finely chop the ginger. Peel and coarsely chop 2 cloves of garlic. Thinly slice the scallions, separating the white bottoms from the hollow green tops. In a bowl, combine the sliced cabbage, chopped ginger, chopped garlic and sliced white parts of the scallions. In a separate bowl, whisk together the coconut aminos, maple syrup, half of the sesame oil and 1 tablespoon of water.

Cook the veggies and finish the quinoa: In a medium skillet (nonstick, if you have one), heat the remaining sesame oil over medium-high heat until hot. Add the sliced carrots and mushroom pieces in an even layer. Cook, without stirring, for 2 to 3 minutes or until lightly browned. Add the prepared cabbage mixture; season with salt (optional) and pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 2 to 3 minutes, or until softened. Add the vinegar. Cook, stirring frequently, for 30 seconds to 1 minute, or until the liquid has evaporated. Transfer to the pot of cooked quinoa; stir to combine. Cover to keep warm. Rinse and wipe out the skillet.

Cook the tofu and serve your dish: Transfer the pressed tofu to a cutting board; cut it lengthwise into 4 equal-size pieces. Season with salt (optional) and pepper on both sides. In the same skillet, heat 2 teaspoons of olive oil over medium-high heat until hot. Add the seasoned tofu pieces in an even layer and cook for 5 to 6 minutes, or until browned. Flip and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, or until lightly browned. Add half of the glaze (carefully, as the liquid may splatter) and cook, frequently spooning the glaze over the tofu, for 1 to 2 minutes, or until the tofu is coated. Transfer to a cutting board. Cut crosswise into 1-inch pieces. Serve the finished quinoa topped with the cooked tofu and the remaining glaze. Garnish with the sliced green tips of the scallions and the furikake. Enjoy!

title: Grilled Fruit with Vanilla Yogurt Cream
description: Grilling caramelizes the natural sugars in fruit, giving it a richer, sweeter flavor that tastes more like dessert than a healthy snack. We are using a combination of peaches, plums and apricots, but any 6 summer stone fruits will do. For even more flavor, we top the fruit with low-fat yogurt and a light drizzle of honey. For extra crunch, try topping with chopped nuts; pistachios work particularly well. This recipe appeared in:
steps: Place the peaches, plums and apricots on the grill, cut side down. Grill over low or indirect heat until soft, about 2 to 4 minutes per side.
Place the fruit on a serving platter and top evenly with yogurt, ground flaxseed and ground almonds.
Drizzle honey over each serving and garnish with a pinch of cinnamon. If desired, sprinkle chopped pistachios over each one. Serve immediately.

title: Peach Pesto Pizza
description: This simple recipe combines three of our favorite P's: pesto, peach and pizza. If you love sweet and savory and are looking for a creative gluten-free pizza recipe with a cauliflower crust to mix up at home, look no further. This recipe is brought to you by CAULIPOWER®, a proud supporter of the American Diabetes Association® and the Diabetes Food Hub®.
steps: Preheat the oven to 425°F (218°C).
Remove your CAULIPOWER® pizza crust from the box and plastic wrapping, and place it on a clean surface.
Spread the pesto sauce evenly over the CAULIPOWER® pizza crust.
Top with peach, fennel, red onion and parmesan and bake for 13 to 16 minutes.
Remove it from the oven and add arugula and sliced almonds, and drizzle balsamic glaze over the pizza.

title: Greek Roasted Eggplant with Feta Cheese
ingredients: 2 eggplant (each cut lengthwise into quarters, stems removed)
steps: Preheat the oven to 400° F. In a small bowl, mix the marinara sauce, lemon juice, oil, garlic and cinnamon. Place the eggplant wedges, skin side down, on a baking sheet lined with unbleached parchment paper. Generously brush the flesh of the eggplant wedges with the marinara mixture.
Roast the eggplant wedges until well cooked and soft, about 30 minutes.
Transfer the wedges to a plate. Sprinkle with parsley, mint, feta cheese and lemon zest and serve.

title: Creamy Chicken Basil Pasta
description: In the mood for a comforting plate of pasta? Try making this diabetes-friendly creamy chicken basil pasta. The homemade sauce made with fresh herbs adds a burst of flavor that will make this recipe a family favorite.
ingredients: 1/4 cup fresh basil (¼ cup fresh basil leaves, cut into thin strips)
1/4 cup parmesan cheese (¼ cup freshly grated parmesan cheese)
2 cups whole wheat penne pasta (2 cups cooked whole wheat pasta)
1 lbs boneless, skinless chicken breasts (1 pound boneless, skinless chicken breasts, cut in half lengthwise into thin cutlets)
1/2 tsp no-salt-added Italian seasoning (½ teaspoon low-sodium or no-salt-added Italian seasoning)
1/2 cup low-fat Italian cheese (½ cup Italian cheese)
3 cups fat-free milk (3 cups skim milk)
1/2 tsp onion powder (½ teaspoon onion powder)
3 tbsp olive oil (3 tablespoons olive oil, divided)
1/2 cup fresh parsley (½ cup packed flat-leaf Italian parsley)
1 cup fresh basil (1 cup packed basil leaves)
5 oz baby spinach (5 oz baby spinach)
steps: Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Add the baby spinach to the pot and blanch for 1 minute. Use a slotted spoon to remove the spinach and place it in a bowl of ice water. Add the packed parsley and basil to the pot and blanch for 15 seconds. Remove and add to the bowl of ice water. Drain the water and squeeze as much liquid as possible from the greens.
Add the spinach, parsley and basil to a food processor. Add the half-and-half to the food processor and puree. Set aside.
Heat a saucepan over medium heat. Add 2 tablespoons of olive oil, garlic and onion powder. Add the flour and whisk for 1 minute. Add the milk and whisk until smooth.
Add the cheese, Italian seasoning, salt (optional) and pepper. Stir until the sauce thickens.
Add the vegetable puree and stir to combine.
Meanwhile, heat a large skillet over medium heat. Add the remaining olive oil. Cook the chicken for 3-4 minutes on each side, until browned and cooked through.
To serve, divide the chicken and pasta among plates. Top with sauce, parmesan cheese and fresh basil strips.

title: Gluten-Free Almond Flour Pancakes
description: Enjoy your morning with these gluten-free almond flour pancakes that provide enough protein to keep you energized. If your diabetes management meal plan allows it, top them with fresh banana slices or low-carb berries.
steps: In a bowl, mix the almond flour, coconut flour, baking powder and salt.
In a separate container, beat the eggs and add the almond milk, 1 tablespoon of olive oil, the maple syrup and the vanilla extract. Mix well.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and stir until combined. Let the batter rest for a couple of minutes to thicken.
Heat a skillet or griddle over medium heat and grease with 1 teaspoon of olive oil or cooking spray.
Pour ¼ cup of batter into the skillet for each pancake. Spread the batter slightly with the back of a spoon.
Cook until bubbles form on the surface, then flip and cook until the other side is golden.
Repeat with the remaining batter.

title: Chicken and Butter Lettuce Wrap
description: LETTUCE present your new healthier favorite chicken wrap! Made with CAULIPOWER BAKED (never fried) chicken tenders, this tasty recipe is gluten-free, dairy-free and packed with protein, making your weekday lunch a little more CAULIPOWERful! This recipe is presented by CAULIPOWER®, a proud supporter of the American Diabetes Association® and Diabetes Food Hub®.
steps: Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F.
Place the CAULIPOWER chicken tenders on a baking sheet that has been sprayed with nonstick cooking spray.
Heat for 17 to 19 minutes for a conventional oven, 15 to 17 minutes for a convection oven, or until the tenders reach an internal temperature of 165 degrees F.
Remove the tenders from the oven and place the hot tenders on the lettuce.
Top with carrots, green onions, avocado, red cabbage and pico de gallo.
